column5: How to use the guide: 2 passes (understand then practice); how to study one lesson (read story, cover answers, do practice, check); what the exam looks like (multiple choice, tables given — list what the booklet contains: binomial, Poisson, Z positive/negative pages, t, chi-square); calculator skills checklist (square root, x², brackets, memory, e^x, nCr, fraction to decimal, rounding to 4 decimals); suggested day-by-day schedule for 3–5 days; rules for when you are stuck. No formulas taught here.

The whole course as ONE story with one running example (a factory filling water bottles: count defective bottles = binomial; defects per hour = Poisson; fill volume = normal; take a sample of 36 bottles = sampling distribution; estimate the true mean fill = confidence interval; check the claim that the average is 500 ml = hypothesis test). Text diagram CH4 -> CH5 -> CH6 -> CH7 with the lesson file for each box. The big question each chapter answers in 1 plain sentence. End with a 6-question quiz "which chapter/lesson is this question from?" in details. Exempt from the lesson template, but needs ## เป้าหมาย and details.

Only the math this course needs, from zero: decimals/percent/fractions (5% = 0.05), powers and square roots, order of operations with fractions inside a root, Σ notation with a 4-number example, factorial and 0!=1, combinations nCr with calculator steps, e and e^(−x) on a calculator, Thai inequality words (อย่างน้อย ≥, อย่างมาก/ไม่เกิน ≤, มากกว่า >, น้อยกว่า <, ระหว่าง), rounding rules, mean of a list, variance with n vs n−1 (mechanics only), unit conversion (month to week, feet to inches). At least 12 drill questions with answers.

What probability is (0 to 1), complement 1−P, independent events multiply, random variable X as "a number we do not know yet", discrete (counts) vs continuous (measurements; probability = area under a curve; P(X=a)=0 so < and ≤ give the same answer), probability distribution table, expected value E(X)=μ, variance σ², SD σ=√σ², what μ and σ mean in plain words. Small examples with a die and a coin. Prepares the reader for CH4.

column5: Discrete uniform (นิยาม 4.1, ทฤษฎี 4.1) and Bernoulli (นิยาม 4.2–4.3, ทฤษฎี 4.2). EX 4.1, 4.2, 4.3. Flag ⚠️ p-05 μ=1/k typo and the p-11 EX 4.3 ambiguity about which outcome is X=1.

Binomial: 4 conditions (fixed n, 2 outcomes, same p, independent), formula with nCx, mean np, variance np(1−p). HOW TO READ THE CUMULATIVE BINOMIAL TABLE P(X≤r), with a translation table turning P(X=r), P(X≥r), P(X>r), P(X<r), P(a≤X≤b) into table values. EX 4.4–4.7. Flag the "3.3" heading typo.

Poisson: counts per time/area, λ, rescaling λ to the asked interval (month to week), formula, mean = variance = λ, reading the cumulative Poisson table (note λ column spacing changes), binomial ≈ Poisson when n large and p small (λ=np, ทฤษฎี 4.5). EX 4.8–4.12. Flag the EX 4.9 weeks-per-month and EX 4.12 draws-per-year assumptions.

Continuous uniform on (a,b): probability = length/(b−a), mean, variance. Exponential: waiting time, survival P(X>x), mean, variance — use the slide parameterisation exactly (check the p-33/p-34 images). Probability as area (rectangle / curve), no integration needed beyond the given results. EX 4.13–4.16 (EX 4.14 uses conditional probability: explain it from zero).

Normal curve properties, 68-95-99.7 rule, standardising Z=(X−μ)/σ, the exam Z table P(Z<z) (positive page and negative page), all area shapes (left, right, between two values, outside, symmetric ±z), reverse lookup (area to z, choose nearest value). EX 4.17 and EX 4.20 fully. Flag EX 4.20(4) as underspecified.

Normal word problems: units (5 ฟุต 2 นิ้ว into inches), "how many pieces" = N × probability, finding a cut-off value from a percentage (warranty problem: x = μ + zσ). EX 4.18, 4.19, 4.21. A reusable 5-step recipe for any normal word problem.
